question: An engineer claims that Longformer, Big Bird and FlashAttention all make the original Transformer’s attention linear by dropping token-to-token connections. Is that correct? Starting from the original Transformer’s complexity and maximum path length, explain how Longformer’s window, dilation and global tokens change connectivity; what Big Bird adds and what its theoretical guarantees require; and why FlashAttention’s tiling and recomputation preserve exact attention without making its arithmetic linear. Distinguish arithmetic, memory and memory-access costs, then recommend an approach when every token pair must still interact. Cite the scanned papers with file and line ranges. Keep the answer within 800 words.

docfoo.answer_markdown:
The claim is only partly correct. Longformer and BigBird sparsify the attention pattern, so they reduce attention arithmetic by omitting many token-to-token connections. FlashAttention does **not** drop connections: it computes exact, full attention while reducing memory use and high-bandwidth-memory (HBM) traffic. [Papers/longformer/content.md:87-87] [Papers/flash-attention/content.md:105-159]

In the original Transformer, full self-attention has \(O(n^2)\) time and memory complexity in sequence length \(n\). Every token can attend directly to every other token, so the maximum attention-path length is 1. [Papers/longformer/content.md:13-39] [Papers/attention-is-all-you-need/content.md:117-123]

Longformer replaces full attention with local sliding-window attention plus task-selected global attention. With window width \(w\), each token attends to \(w/2\) tokens on each side; the local computation is \(O(n \times w)\), and the receptive field grows across layers. Dilation spaces out the window connections, increasing receptive field without increasing computation; for fixed dilation \(d\) and \(w\), the stated receptive field is \(\ell \times d \times w\) over \(\ell\) layers. Global attention is symmetric: global tokens attend to the whole sequence, and all tokens attend to them. This supplies long-range routes, with combined local/global attention still \(O(n)\) when the number of global tokens is small and independent of \(n\). [Papers/longformer/content.md:91-117]

BigBird combines local-window, random, and global connections. Its global tokens can be existing tokens (ITC) or additional tokens (ETC); the paper says the added ETC tokens provide extra context storage and improve performance in experiments. [Papers/big-bird/content.md:15-41] [Papers/big-bird/content.md:97-101] Its theoretical claims are conditional: the universality result uses a sparse graph containing a star graph, and the Turing-completeness result is for a sparse attention mechanism using \(O(n)\) inner products, under the paper’s stated precision assumptions. [Papers/big-bird/content.md:718-730] [Papers/big-bird/content.md:793-799] These are expressivity guarantees, not a claim that sparse attention reproduces every full-attention computation at the same cost.

FlashAttention instead tiles \(Q,K,V\), computes attention block by block, and combines block results using normalization statistics. It avoids storing the \(O(N^2)\) intermediate attention matrices: the paper states \(O(N)\) additional memory beyond inputs and output. For the backward pass, it recomputes attention intermediates from stored inputs, output, and statistics rather than storing them. The result remains exact, with \(O(N^2d)\) FLOPs; tiling and recomputation target HBM accesses, not quadratic arithmetic. [Papers/flash-attention/content.md:105-159]

So the costs differ: Longformer and BigBird reduce arithmetic by using sparse connectivity; FlashAttention preserves quadratic arithmetic and all-pairs interaction, while reducing additional memory and HBM traffic. If every token pair must still interact, use **FlashAttention**: it retains exact attention rather than approximating it by dropping connections. [Papers/flash-attention/content.md:105-159]

The evidence gives complexity and connectivity descriptions but does not state a numeric maximum path length for Longformer or BigBird; those depend on the specific attention pattern and layers. It also does not provide source file line ranges in a form usable here, so citations identify the evidence blocks rather than file/line ranges.

sources.section: [FA] 3.1 An Efficient Attention Algorithm With Tiling and Recomputation
[BB] Question Answering (QA) We considered following four challenging datasets:
[BB] Big Bird: Transformers for Longer Sequences
[BB] A.2.2 Contextual Mappings and Sparse Attention Mechanisms (part 1/2)
[BB] A.2.3 Approximating modified Transformers by Transformers
[AI] 3.2.3 Applications of Attention in our Model
[BB] A.2.2 Contextual Mappings and Sparse Attention Mechanisms (part 2/2)

agentic.answer_markdown:
The claim is **only partly correct**. Longformer and BigBird reduce attention’s arithmetic by restricting which token pairs interact. **FlashAttention does not drop pairs**: it computes exact dense attention, reducing memory traffic and memory use, not the quadratic attention arithmetic.

**Baseline.** Original self-attention has \(O(n^2d)\) computation per layer, \(O(1)\) sequential operations, and maximum path length \(O(1)\): every position can directly reach every other in one layer. Restricting it to a neighborhood of size \(r\) lowers the tabulated cost to \(O(rnd)\), but raises maximum path length to \(O(n/r)\). [attention-is-all-you-need/content.md:147-147] The paper explains that shorter dependency paths can help learning long-range dependencies. [attention-is-all-you-need/content.md:167-169]

**Longformer.** A fixed sliding window lets each token attend only nearby positions. Stacked layers expand the receptive field, so distant tokens can influence one another indirectly, rather than through a single direct connection. [longformer/content.md:91-91] Dilation inserts gaps in that window, increasing receptive field without increasing computation; with fixed dilation \(d\), window \(w\), and \(\ell\) layers, the paper gives receptive field \(\ell dw\). [longformer/content.md:101-103] Neither local nor dilated attention alone guarantees direct all-pairs access in one layer. Longformer adds *symmetric* global attention at selected tokens: global tokens attend to all positions, and all positions attend to them. These hubs provide a route between distant tokens, but do not make every ordinary token pair directly connected. [longformer/content.md:107-107]

**BigBird.** BigBird combines a local window, a fixed number of random connections per query, and global tokens. [big-bird/content.md:101-101] This adds random long-range links to local structure and global routes; it remains sparse rather than restoring the full attention matrix. Its universal-approximation result has a specific condition: the attention graph must contain a star graph (enabled by global connectivity); it is not an unconditional claim that any sparse pattern matches full attention. [big-bird/content.md:123-125] The Turing-completeness result also assumes standard precision conditions, as the paper’s summary states. [big-bird/content.md:37-37] The paper also notes a “no free lunch”: some tasks solved by full attention in constant layers require near-linear-in-\(n\) layers for sufficiently sparse mechanisms, under stated complexity assumptions. [big-bird/content.md:151-159]

**FlashAttention.** Tiling loads blocks of \(Q,K,V\) into fast SRAM and accumulates correctly normalized partial results; recomputation in the backward pass avoids storing the full attention matrix. This preserves exact attention. [flash-attention/content.md:107-107] [flash-attention/content.md:131-133] Its attention arithmetic remains quadratic in sequence length; its benefit is fewer HBM reads/writes and linear memory footprint, not linear FLOPs. The paper reports quadratic runtime growth, but linear memory growth. [flash-attention/content.md:285-287] It also gives subquadratic HBM-access complexity for its tiled algorithm. [flash-attention/content.md:173-175]

**Recommendation:** if every token pair must interact, use exact dense attention with FlashAttention (or an equivalent IO-aware implementation). It preserves all pairwise interactions while reducing memory-access overhead and avoiding quadratic intermediate storage; it does **not** eliminate quadratic arithmetic. [flash-attention/content.md:31-33]
